findings.evidence: The finance liaison reviews the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time.
findings.violation: Three different terms, benefits team, finance liaison, and people operations office, are each used as the actor who tracks or reviews the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year, with no signal that they name the same role; this passage names finance liaison as the reviewer in its first sentence, then benefits team in its second, so the two terms sit inside the same two-sentence paragraph with nothing marking them as synonyms.
findings.fix: Pick one name for the role that reviews the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year, for example the benefits team, and use it consistently in Program Overview, Special Cases, and Questions and Updates, or state explicitly that finance liaison and people operations office are different names for the same team.

instances.evidence: The benefits team tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time.
The people operations office tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit.

findings.evidence: 71-word sentence, 5 subordinate-clause markers: Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk that the standard equipment list assumes every applicant has for the whole benefit year while the finance office tracks the second device against the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes for each category.
findings.violation: The sentence runs to 71 words with 5 subordinate-clause markers, longer than the reader can hold in mind on a single pass.
findings.fix: Split the sentence at a subordinate-clause boundary.

findings.evidence: The determination of stipend eligibility happens before any payment goes out. The escalation of repeat requests happens automatically within the same quarter.
findings.violation: Both sentences in this section name an abstraction, the determination and the escalation, as the grammatical subject instead of the person or team who actually determines eligibility or escalates repeat requests, so a reader cannot tell who is responsible for either action.
findings.fix: Name the actor as the subject: for example, the benefits team determines stipend eligibility before any payment goes out, and the benefits team escalates repeat requests automatically within the same quarter.

findings.evidence: 71-word sentence: Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk that the standard equipment list assumes every applicant has for the whole benefit year while the finance office tracks the second device against the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes for each category.
findings.violation: At 71 words, with 0 comma-set-off clause(s) and 5 subordinate-clause marker(s), the sentence stacks interruptions between its subject and its main verb instead of holding the main clause together.
findings.fix: Move subordinate clauses and modifiers after the main clause, not between its subject and verb.

findings.evidence: Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk that the standard equipment list assumes every applicant has for the whole benefit year while the finance office tracks the second device against the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes for each category.
findings.violation: The sentence's newest and most important content, that fieldwork employees can qualify for a second device, lands in the middle of the sentence, while the final position is occupied by the annual amount the equipment catalog already publishes for each category, information the reader already has from the rest of the policy, so the position that carries the most weight is spent on old material instead of the new exception.
findings.fix: End the sentence on the fieldwork second-device exception itself, and move the restatement of the annual tracked amount earlier or into a separate sentence.

findings.evidence: The reviewer confirms the workspace address matches the address already on file with payroll. ... The reviewer logs every workspace confirmation in the same shared tracking sheet the benefits team maintains.
findings.violation: This paragraph interleaves conditions the employee reader must satisfy, such as where the workspace sits or whether it is shared, with sentences describing the reviewer's own internal process, such as confirming the address against payroll or logging confirmations to a shared tracking sheet, without separating the two audiences' content, so the employee reader has to sort out which sentences describe their own eligibility and which describe an internal administrative step.
findings.fix: Move the reviewer's internal process steps, address confirmation against payroll and logging to the shared tracking sheet, into a separate note or an internal-process appendix, and keep this paragraph to the conditions the employee needs to satisfy.

findings.evidence: In addition, eligibility for the workspace stipend depends on several details the reviewer checks one at a time.
findings.violation: This paragraph names the benefit the workspace stipend, while the title and the rest of the document call it the home-office equipment stipend or simply the stipend, with no signal that workspace stipend names the same benefit rather than a second, separate one.
findings.fix: Use the same term, for example the stipend or the home-office equipment stipend, throughout, including in this paragraph's opening sentence.

findings.evidence: Employees must submit the receipt, the manager's approval form, and the original purchase order before the review begins.
findings.violation: The sentence embeds three or more comma- or semicolon-separated parallel items inline rather than presenting them as a formatted list.
findings.fix: Reformat the inline items as a numbered or bulleted list.

findings.evidence: Additionally, employees shall retain receipts for one year after the purchase date.
findings.violation: The sentence states a binding requirement using shall or an indirect requirement phrasing instead of must.

findings.evidence: The finance office conducts an evaluation of every submitted receipt before it approves the amount.
findings.violation: The action is buried inside the noun 'evaluation', carried by a generic support verb, instead of stated as the sentence's own main verb.
findings.fix: Restate the nominalized noun as the sentence's main verb.
